title: Lalita's two addresses
hookLine: goddesses of speech compose a thousand names, and two of them are addresses
carry: one goddess, on the altar and within
tomorrow: the sleeper wakes at the bottom of the road. where is she going?

lines: A TEACHER HOLDS ONE THING BACK.
THE GODDESSES OF SPEECH COMPOSE IT.
cards: In the Brahmanda Purana, the sage Agastya studies with Hayagriva, the horse-headed form of Vishnu, and hears the story of the Goddess Lalita. One thing his teacher holds back: her thousand names.
When Agastya finally asks, Hayagriva tells him where they came from. The Goddess herself commanded the goddesses of speech to compose them, and they sang the names before her whole court.
That's the Lalita Sahasranama, still chanted in homes and temples. And tucked among the thousand names are two addresses.

teach.b: Near the end, she's Sri Chakra Raja Nilaya: she whose home is the Sri Chakra, the king of chakras. That's the Sri Yantra, this week's first map, which is also called the Sri Chakra. Chakra: a wheel, a circle.

teach.h: HER HOME: THE ROOT, AS KUNDALINI.
teach.b: And early in the list, another run of names places her in the body: she who dwells in the Muladhara, the root, and, simply, Kundalini.
Same Goddess. Two addresses. This is the Shakta teaching the week has been climbing toward: the Goddess worshipped on the altar's diagram is the same power coiled at the base of every person.
That's why one word, chakra, names both maps.

teach.h: THE WEEK, BACK FOR ONE PASS.
teach.b: Look back and the week falls into place. Pusalar's temple in the mind, and the Bhavana Upanishad: the worshipper is the map. Jagannath's unfinished wood: the presence is invited, not bought.
Bhrigu's layers: more of you than flesh. Kundalini asleep at the root. Indra at the water: the atman isn't the body in the mirror.
And at the heart, a sound nothing strikes. So when someone asks why a Hindu grandmother bows to a brass diagram and also sits in silence with her eyes closed, it's one worship.
She's visiting the same Goddess at both addresses.

how: The Lalita Sahasranama, the thousand names of the Goddess Lalita, is chanted in homes and temples, especially in Sri Vidya, where the Sri Yantra is also called the Sri Chakra; the chakras of the body are approached in meditation, usually with a teacher.

games.q: what does “the chakras as a map” mean?
o: circles on a map, made to be traveled
a set of rainbow stickers for posters
spinning organs found along the spine

games.q: one Goddess, two addresses — tap the pairs.
p: her home is the king of chakras
one of her names: coiled at the root

s: the Sri Yantra is also called the Sri Chakra
chakra, a wheel or circle, names both maps.
in the Lalita Sahasranama, the Goddess's names place her only in temples
one name gives the Sri Chakra as her home; others place her in the body, at the root, as Kundalini.
what makes an altar yantra holy is the metal it's cast in
it's the rite of prana pratishtha and the worship after it.

games.q: a friend says the Sri Chakra and the chakras of the body have nothing to do with each other. what's the best reply from this week?
o: one Goddess lives in both: her names give the Sri Chakra and the root of the body.
they're one object: drawn on brass, and also hidden in your organs.
they share a name by accident, and that's all there is.
games.why: the Lalita Sahasranama names her home as the Sri Chakra, and also names her Kundalini, dwelling at the root. chakra, a wheel, names both maps.

practice: If you pray, say three of the Goddess's names slowly, with a breath between: Lalita. Sri Chakra Raja Nilaya. Kundalini.

Feel where each one lands, out on the altar or here within. If you don't pray, say the week's lines instead, worship in the mind is real, invited not bought, more than flesh, and sit with the one that stayed.

wordCard.voice: The chakras as a map: wheels, circles, centers. One word names the body's lotuses and the Sri Chakra, and one Goddess lives in both.

orig.note: Sanskrit: the auspicious wheel; another name for the Sri Yantra.

carryVoice: Last line of the week: one Goddess, on the altar and within. Two addresses, one road.

sources.ref: Lalita Sahasranama, in the Brahmanda Purana (Hayagriva teaches Agastya; the names composed by the goddesses of speech at the Goddess's command); the names Shrichakrarajanilaya (she whose abode is the Sri Chakra), Muladharaikanilaya and Kundalini

the week's sources, recalled: Periya Puranam (Pusalar); Bhavana Upanishad; the Jagannath legend; Taittiriya Upanishad 2–3; Hatha Yoga Pradipika, chapters 3–4; Chandogya Upanishad 8.7–8.12; Sat-Cakra-Nirupana; 1 Kings 19:11–12
